stem:
The diagram shows Yamini's square courtyard tile. Its area is $1296\,\mathrm{cm}^{2}$. She writes the prime factorisation $1296 = 2^{4} \times 3^{4}$ and asks whether $1296$ is a perfect square and, if it is, what its square root is.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: $1296$ is a perfect square because the primes split into two identical groups $2^{2} \times 3^{2}$ and $2^{2} \times 3^{2}$, so $\sqrt{1296} = 36$.
Report the words factor pair as the square root of $1296$.
The square root $36$ produces the prime factorisation $2^{4} \times 3^{4}$, so she starts from $36$ instead of pairing the primes.
Read $1296$ as a perfect cube and take its cube root instead of pairing the prime factors.

teacher.key_rationale: All exponents in 2^4×3^4 are even, so the primes pair into two groups each equal to 2^2×3^2=36, and √1296=36. Naming factor pair, starting from the root instead of pairing, or switching to cube roots all miss the perfect-square hinge.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source grid quadrilateral as a labelled square courtyard tile with area 1296 cm².
